attribution_limitations: The dynamic compliance unit is printed as ml/cmH_(2)0, with a zero as the final character; every other pressure unit in the case text is cmH_(2)O. The unit is kept as printed and the zero is probably a one-character print artefact for cmH2O.

The pneumothorax is called right-sided apical on chest radiography and in the Figure 2 caption of the chest CT, but right-sided ventral in the case-text description of the same chest CT; the source does not reconcile the site words.
Barotrauma is stated as a developed complication in the abstract but as the most likely cause in the case text.

The reference point of "2 days later" is not named and the sentence opens a new paragraph after the sedation and pressure support adjustment, so no order is taken from it. The order of the transpulmonary pressure measurement before the imaging rests only on the Discussion sentence "transpulmonary pressure measurements before detection of gross barotrauma".

Whether the antibiotics added to conservative treatment were administered is not separately stated; the source says conservative treatment with addition of antibiotics was chosen, followed by gradual improvement.

claims.text: A 67-year-old man with a past medical history of hypertension was admitted to the ICU with hypoxemic respiratory failure due to severe COVID-19 pneumonitis. He had been admitted to the hospital 2 days earlier with dyspnea and fever for 2 weeks. Laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and decreased lymphocytes, SARS-CoV-2 PCR was positive, and chest radiography showed bilateral diffuse opacities. He was treated with cefotaxime.

claims.text: Without respiratory improvement, chest radiography showed a right-sided apical pneumothorax that was not present on an X-ray 3 days earlier. Chest CT confirmed a right-sided ventral pneumothorax, subcutaneous emphysema up to the left side of the neck and extensive pneumomediastinum, with no airway injury, so barotrauma was considered the most likely cause. Conservative treatment with added antibiotics was chosen, respiratory status gradually improved, and he had a tracheostomy and was weaned off the ventilator.
